Methylmercury contamination is known to affect fetal neural 
development disproportionately. It crosses the placenta and 
blood-brain barrier and accumulates in the fetus; cord blood 
levels are 70% higher than maternal levels (Cox and Phelan, 
2009b).
Traces of methylmercury are found in most fish, but concen-
trations are highest in those fish that are large and predatory.
